newsitem.title: UK: Bakyrchik shares stage modest recovery.
newsitem.headline: Bakyrchik shares stage modest recovery.

text.p: Shares in London-listed Russian gold miner Bakyrchik Gold Plc continued to stage a modest recovery from their recent collapse in value, on Friday, traders said.

Shares in the company, which recently lost control of its main asset, a gold mine in Kazakhstan, as part of a refinancing package, were up 26 percent to 54 pence in mid-morning trading, after touching a high of 60 pence.
One market maker in the stock said buying was mostly by small private clients.
"It is scrappy buying," he said. "It is just buying at the bottom."
Bakyrchik shares were trading well above five stg each in the middle of 1996, but have slid steadily since, touching a low of just 12 pence each on July 25.

Last month, Indochina Goldfields Ltd, its biggest shareholder, stepped in with a rescue package for the debt-ridden operation, increasing its stake in the Kazakhstan gold mine to 80 percent from 15 percent.
Bakyrchik will lose its London listing when the package is finally approved.
